paragraphs: Friend, here's what I love. Hezekiah gets the worst news a man can get, and he doesn't argue with the messenger or go hide in his pantry. He turns his face to the wall and talks to the LORD, and he weeps bitterly (2 Kings 20:2-3). That's your invitation, baker: when the news is heavy, you can take it straight to God.

And look at how God answers. Before Isaiah has even left the middle courtyard, the word of the LORD comes (2 Kings 20:4). Then God says, "I have heard your prayer; I have seen your tears." (2 Kings 20:5). Your prayers are not floating off into nowhere. He hears every one, and He sees every tear.

Then God does more than Hezekiah asked. He says, "I will add fifteen years to your life," and He promises to deliver the city too (2 Kings 20:6). When Hezekiah wants a sign, the LORD even brings the shadow back ten steps (2 Kings 20:11). Friend, that's the God you're baking for, so keep praying and keep that oven warm. Hezekiah's story isn't over yet.
